title: Total habitat is not reachable habitat
hook: Compare a large connected component with a smaller accessible fragment.

doesNotKnow: Distinguish supplied accessible habitat from all habitat in an area.

misconception: Equal total habitat guarantees equal reachable habitat.
objective: Distinguish supplied accessible habitat from all habitat in an area.

claims.text: Habitat isolation can matter in addition to total habitat area.
David Quammen, The Song of the Dodo (1996)
The large component permits {A}; the accessible fragment caps reach at {B}. Component sizes are supplied premises, not inferred from a geographic map.
Does it hold up? This is a capped tree, not animal movement, general habitat connectivity or extinction risk.
claims.source: {"type":"source-access-hold","note":"No empirical effect or research verdict established. Only bounded arithmetic proposed."}

recall.question: An area has 40 cells but the organism’s connected component has 9. Can more tree rounds alone justify counting 40?
recall.why: The accessible component caps reach unless a connection is added.
